topic: Valuation of property, depreciation, and related financial concepts

questions.q: 51. Evaluation of building is done based on
questions.explain: Preliminary evaluation of a building's cost is typically calculated using the plinth area rate of similar structures in the locality.

questions.q: 63. *Compound amount of Rs. 100 in 4 years @ 4% interest
questions.explain: Using A = P(1 + r/100)^n, 100(1.04)^4 is approximately 116.98, rounded to 117.

questions.q: 95. *Contractor profit is added to
questions.explain: Contractor's profit is included during the rate analysis phase for individual items.

questions.q: 151. The life of teak wood doors and window is usually taken to be
questions.explain: The average service life of high-quality teak wood joinery in buildings is estimated at 40 years before significant decay or structural replacement is required.

questions.q: 165. The technique of finding the fair price of an existing building or property is known as
questions.explain: Valuation is the process of determining the present-day value of an asset, whereas estimation is predicting the cost before construction.

questions.q: 166. Valuation is done for
questions.explain: The primary goal of valuation is to find the actual present value of the property in its current condition and market context.

questions.q: 181. Working out the exact quantities of various items of work is known as
questions.explain: Quantity Surveying is the professional discipline of calculating materials, labor, and costs for construction projects.

questions.q: 187. The value of the property or structures become less by its becoming out of date in style is known as
questions.explain: Obsolescence is the loss in value due to changes in design, technology, or demand, making the property 'outdated'.

questions.q: 188. The value of the property (without being dismentaled) at the end of the useful life period is known as
questions.explain: Salvage value is the value of an asset at the end of its utility without being broken up. (Note: Question text says 'salvation' which is a typo for 'salvage').

questions.q: 189. The annual periodic payments made for the repayment of the capital invested is known as
questions.explain: An annuity is a fixed sum of money paid to someone each year, often used to repay capital over a period of time.

questions.q: 190. The net annual letting out value of a property, which is obtained after deducting the amount of yearly repairs from the gross income, is known as
questions.explain: Rateable value is used by local authorities to calculate taxes, determined by deducting outgoings from gross rent.

questions.q: 191. The value shown in account book after allowing necessary depreciation known as
questions.explain: Book value is the original cost minus accumulated depreciation as recorded in accounting ledgers.

questions.q: 192. The gradual accumulations of amount by way of annual periodic deposits which is meant for the replacement of the structure at the end of its useful life period is known as
questions.explain: A sinking fund is created by setting aside a specific sum annually so that the accumulated amount can replace the asset at the end of its life.

questions.q: 193. The value of the dismentalled material less the cost of dismentalling is called
questions.explain: Scrap value is the worth of the materials (bricks, steel, timber) after the building has been demolished.

questions.q: 208. If the payment of annuity beings after some years in future, it is known as
questions.explain: An annuity where payments start after a specific number of years or a certain period has elapsed is called a deferred annuity.

questions.q: 209. Salvage value of any structure is
questions.explain: Salvage value is the value of a property at the end of its utility period without being dismantled, which is typically higher than scrap value (value of dismantled materials).

questions.q: 215. The amount of capital from required to be invested to receive a net annual income as an annuity of Rs. 1 /- at certain rate of interest is called
questions.explain: Year's Purchase (YP) is the capital sum required to be invested to receive an annuity of Re 1.00 at a given rate of interest.

questions.q: 216. Find the value of year's purchase to get Rs.1 per year at the interest rate of 5%.
questions.explain: Year's Purchase = 100 / Interest Rate. Here, 100 / 5 = 20.00.

questions.q: 221. Value is
questions.explain: Value is the present worth of a property, which can differ from the historical cost.

questions.q: 227. The value of structure without being dismantled at the end of its utility period is known as:
questions.explain: The value of a property at the end of its useful life, without being dismantled, is the salvage (or savage) value.

questions.q: 230. If the net income is calculated with the rental method of valuation then, the net income is then,
options: a difference of gross income with all outgoing expenses
a product of actual cost and depreciation
a addition of original cost and annual depreciation
a difference of original cost and scrap-
questions.explain: Net Income = Gross Rent - Outgoings (taxes, repairs, management, etc.).

questions.q: 232. The sinking fund is:
options: a part of the proceed in reserve for additional structure and modification
the sum of money to be paid to authorities by the tenants
the fund for rebuilding structure its economic life is over
raised to meet the maintenance costs of the structure before dismantling
questions.explain: A sinking fund is a fund created by setting aside annual installments so that at the end of the utility period, the accumulated amount is enough to replace the structure.

questions.q: 237. Purpose of valuation is
questions.explain: Valuation is required for various purposes including sale, tax assessment, and securing bank loans.

questions.q: 239. In a linear depreciation method of property valuation depreciation is imposed on costs related to:
questions.explain: Land does not depreciate; depreciation is applied to the building structure which has a finite life.

questions.q: 241. Annual rent is generally fixed at:
questions.explain: Annual rent is typically estimated between 5% and 10% of the capitalized value of the building.
